title: Mother recalls killings of 4 sons in Davao before Truth Commission
summary: A 72-year-old mother whose four sons were killed in Davao City testified before the Truth Commission on extrajudicial killings on Friday, recounting alleged threats against her children and her…

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 9:22pm

A 72-year-old mother whose four sons were killed in Davao City testified before the Truth Commission on extrajudicial killings on Friday, recounting alleged threats against her children and her decades-long search for justice.
"Kung totoo man na ganoon ang mga anak ko, dapat pinapreso sila, hindi papatayin," Nanay Alia said as translated by an interpreter during the Commission's hearing.
(If the accusations against my children were true, they should have been imprisoned, not killed.)
Nanay Alia said she had been seeking justice for about 25 years for her sons Richard, Christopher, Bobby and Fernando, who were killed when they were still teenagers.
In July 2001, Alia found 18-year-old Richard dead with stab wounds. She said she later learned that Richard had allegedly been threatened by police before his death.
“Sabi ng pulis, isa-isahin niya ang mga anak ko,” Nanay Alia said.
(The police said he would kill my children one by one.)

Christopher was 18 when he was killed in October 2001 also from stab wounds. After a year, Bobby, 14 years old, was killed after his arrest in November 2002. He was later found severely beaten and stabbed. Fernando, 15 years old, was also stabbed and died in April 2007.
Nanay Alia said she believed the Davao Death Squad existed based on what she said she experienced and learned about the deaths of her children.
“Merong mga nagsasabi na hindi naman daw totoo itong mga DDS, yung Davao Death Squad. Hindi, totoo yan. Kasi kilala ko ‘yan sila. Alam ko yung sistema nila,” she said.
(There are those who say that these DDS, the Davao Death Squad, are not real. No, they are real. Because I know them. I know their operation.)

“Isa lang yung nakita ko sa kanila, yung mga anak ko. Yung pagpatay kay Topher o kay Bobby. Yung pumatay sa kanya, dating preso. Ito kasing DDS, isang grupo ng mga pulis na malalaki, matataas ang ranggo. Tapos kukuha sila ng ibang tao. Sila ang papatay. Para sila mismo, safe lang,” she added.

(I only saw one of them, in the case of my children. The killing of Topher or Bobby. The one who killed him was a former prisoner. This is the DDS, a group of big, high-ranking police officers. Then they will hire other people. They will kill. So that they themselves are safe.)
Forensic pathologist Dr. Raquel Fortun said the killings of Alia’s children should have been thoroughly investigated.
Fortun said Christopher had multiple stab wounds to the chest, including injuries affecting the heart and lungs, and a cut on his forearm that could be considered a defensive wound.
“Ibig sabihin, nakapag-react siya noong siya ay inatake. Ito yung tinatawag nating defensive wound,” she said.
(This means he was able to react when he was attacked. This is what we call a defensive wound.)
Richard had facial injuries and a stab wound to the chest that allegedly affected his lung and caused internal bleeding.
Both bodies had reportedly been embalmed before examination.
The records reviewed appeared to have been prepared by one doctor and the reports contained limited information, according to Fortun.
She said the Commission would seek additional records, including the death certificates of Bobby and Fernando, possible autopsy records, and hospital records concerning Fernando.
Fortun said the similar use of sharp force injuries in the four deaths raised questions about whether the killings involved the same assailant or group.

The Truth Commission was organized as an independent, civil society-led body tasked to find out the truth about "drug war" killings in the Philippines, restore dignity to the victims, and foster healing and reform.—LDF, GMA News
